concept: Adaptive block-size scheduling for DFlash at inference
summary: D-cut does not change the drafter's block size; it truncates the verified prefix, so the drafter still runs at full width and only verification shrinks.

facts.text: D-cut does not change the drafter's block size; it truncates the verified prefix, so the drafter still runs at full width and only verification shrinks.
That matches the DFlash paper's finding that draft time is nearly flat in block size for moderate blocks, so truncation saves verify cost and not draft cost.
Feb 2026: DFlash paper (v2 cached) names dynamic block-size scheduling as enabled by large-block training.
30 Apr 2026: DFlash accepted to ICML 2026 (OpenReview forum Oz335dV48X, last modified 22 Sep 2026).
Block 16 unpruned is worse than block 8 under load on dense models: Qwen3.5-27B at concurrency 32 averages 0.94x for block 16 and 1.21x for block 8.
The SGLang DFlash v2 post's sample command and benchmark block size mismatch (already recorded) is explained by this effect: a static choice is concurrency-dependent.
A published adaptive scheduler for DFlash verification depth exists (D-cut, vLLM PR 47131).
D-cut keeps the drafter at full block width and prunes only the verified prefix.
DFlash block 16 averaged 0.94x and block 8 averaged 1.21x of autoregressive throughput on Qwen3.5-27B at concurrency 32.
DFlash's ICML 2026 OpenReview entry lists Jian Chen, Yesheng Liang and Zhijian Liu.

CONTRADICTS: draft-length-tuning-spec-draft-n-max-for-block-d.md Open questions line "the sources show no PR" for adaptive scheduling. D-cut (arXiv 2607.14647, vLLM PR 47131) schedules verified depth per request from drafter confidence and a startup cost table, using DFlash block 16 drafters with D = 15.
